newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-AUSSIE PLAGUED BY RATE DOUBTS AS JOBS LOOM.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-AUSSIE PLAGUED BY RATE DOUBTS AS JOBS LOOM.

text.p: AUS$ S/Term range *Support *Restnce *RSI-14 *MA-10 *MA-20
*Offshore range roughly US$0.7330/7367
*AUD remains under pressure as a late sell order from NY put
paid to a modest bounce and keeps focus on $0.7330 support
*Bears betting July labour data today will be weak enough to
raise the risk of yet another rate cut and force test of $0.7310
*Anything less than forecasted 25,000 jobs rise will be
considered soft. Volatile unemployment rate also bears watching
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the dollar was pinned at US$0.7342/47 having been down as low as US$0.7330 and as high as US$0.7367 offshore after finishing at US$0.7355/60 late here Wednesday.
Traders said bids were still solid beneath US$0.7330 and could yet hold, as they did a fortnight ago when the currency briefly plumbed 18-month lows at US$0.7310.

Chart watchers were far less confident following last week's failed rally to 75 cents, which to many confirmed the four month downtrend from 80 cents still had further to run. They were targetting US$0.7250 as a first stop enroute to the 1995 low and Fibonacci retracement area of US$0.7070/7100.
The retreat could start today if the jobs data were as dire as the bears seemed to expect.

Median forecasts are for employment to rise 25,000 in July which at least would be better than the meagre 11,900 gain made in June. It would not, however, make up for May's shock 40,300 fall or for the 63,900 full-time jobs lost so far this year. And it would leave unemployment stuck around 8.6 percent.

Indeed so poor has the employment performance been that today's figures would have to be astoundingly strong to change consumers' gloomy perceptions about the labour market and promise an improvement in confidence.

All this meant that a result less than 25,000 would be seen as soft and stoke speculation about a cut sooner rather than later, while it would probably take a rise of more than 50,000 to still the easing whispers.
An added complication is the unemployment rate which analysts warn could actually rise sharply if employment is strong since more people may have been looking for work.
Elsewhere, the dollar lost a little ground on the mark and the yen but remained relatively firm and gained on sterling which suffered a steep selloff overnight.
